Apple TV (now $6.99/month for limited time) is primarily home to original shows and movies, but Apple recently started adding fan-favorite classic films too. Here’s what’s new and coming next.

Apple TV recently added 20 beloved classic movies, with more coming soon

Historically, Apple TV has avoided licensing content, instead preferring an all-originals catalog. But one recent exception involves classic movies.

This fall, a new batch of fan-favorite films has debuted every month for Apple TV subscribers.

Here’s the lineup of 20 movies that were recently added for November:

  • Interstellar
  • Minority Report
  • Anchorman
  • Pulp Fiction
  • Rachel Getting Married
  • Talladega Nights
  • Dead Poets Society
  • Get Smart
  • Julie & Julia
  • Arrival
  • Clueless
  • Dave
  • Forrest Gump
  • Bad Boys
  • Eat Pray Love
  • Body of Lies
  • 12 Monkeys
  • The Nice Guys
  • Big
  • Prisoners

Now through a new video on its YouTube channel, Apple has confirmed that even more films are set to debut on December 1.

Joining the Apple TV catalog next month are:

  • Shutter Island, the Martin Scorsese film with Leonardo DiCaprio
  • Friends with Benefits, starring Justin Timberlake and Mila Kunis
  • Magnolia, from director Paul Thomas Anderson
  • Austin Powers: International Man of Mystery, the Mike Myers comedy
  • The Karate Kid, the 1984 classic

Over the last few months, Apple has been adding 15-20 new films each month, so the five titles above are likely just a sampling of what December will bring.

Alongside these licensed films, Apple has started very selectively licensing TV series too. One recent premiere, Small Prophets, is an acclaimed comedy that was hailed as perhaps “the finest show to hit Apple this year.”

Have you been watching any of Apple TV’s classic movie additions? Let us know in the comments.

Apple TV is available for just $6.99/month (over 50% off) for a limited time, with the offer ending Monday, November 30.
